ashe: A Deadlock gang leader who fights with a rifle and explosives.
Aim from cover with The Viper and leave Coach Gun available if a diver reaches you. A useful angle needs an exit as well as a target.
Shoot Dynamite when its explosion can pressure several enemies or force them out of cover. Do not stay scoped when your position is being contested.
Place B.O.B. where his line of fire complements your team's angle. Announce the deployment and watch for abilities that can shut him down.
baptiste: A former Talon medic who now uses his combat training to help people harmed by war.
Choose a position where your healing projectiles can reach the team without exposing you to every enemy sightline. Use Exo Boots to reach useful cover, rather than jumping constantly.
Place Immortality Field where allies can use it and enemies cannot immediately destroy it. Rotate healing and rifle pressure without letting an ally's emergency go unnoticed.
Amplification Matrix needs a usable firing lane. Communicate its position before the fight and do not force teammates to abandon cover just to shoot through it.
bastion: An omnic war machine that became an explorer with an interest in nature.
Use Recon to move between protected positions. Enter Assault when a target will remain in your line of fire, rather than when the whole enemy team can simply hide.
Keep a corner or teammate between you and a coordinated flank. Use the grenade to pressure cover, and leave a retreat route before your high-pressure configuration ends.
Artillery commits your position. Start it from safety and place shots around the enemy's likely movement and escape choices; treat forcing a rotation as useful pressure.
brigitte: An engineer who took up arms to defend others alongside Reinhardt.
Stay near allies who need protection. Use Whip Shot to discourage an approach instead of walking alone into enemy close-range damage.
Manage Repair Packs according to who is under immediate threat. Use your shield and movement to survive a duel while keeping Inspire opportunities safe.
Watch the enemy dive timing and answer it together with your other support. Rally is a team engagement resource; choose a fight your nearby allies can participate in.
cassidy: An outlaw gunslinger who uses a revolver to carry out his own idea of justice.
Take a covered angle where Peacekeeper can threaten the enemy while you remain close enough for teammate help. Avoid chasing mobile targets into isolated routes.
Treat Combat Roll as a resource for survival and a timely reload. Aim to finish a realistic target rather than spending the whole fight shooting a protected tank.
Deadeye announces a threat and exposes your position. Check cover, interruption threats, and escape routes before activating it; forcing enemies away can matter even without an elimination.
doomfist: A former Talon leader who uses a powerful gauntlet and committed movement.
Choose a destination and an exit before using Seismic Slam or Rocket Punch. A deep landing without support is a risk even when the first hit connects.
Use Power Block when enemies have a reason to damage you, and watch for attacks it cannot safely answer. Keep a movement resource to leave after creating pressure.
Coordinate displacement with an ally's line of fire. Meteor Strike can change your position as well as threaten a target; reassess the enemy's defensive resources before landing.
echo: An adaptive omnic created by Overwatch scientist Mina Liao.
Use Flight to reach an angle with cover and a path back to your team. Do not hover in a predictable open sightline just because you can stay airborne.
Combine projectile pressure and Sticky Bombs to make a realistic finishing opportunity for Focusing Beam. If the target receives help, disengage instead of tunneling on the original plan.
Choose a Duplicate target whose abilities you can use well in the current fight. Consider where the copied kit will leave you when the transformation ends.
hanzo: A Shimada archer who seeks a new path after his family's conflict.
Aim at routes enemies actually use and move after revealing your firing position. Wall Climb gives you access to angles, but it does not make an exposed ledge safe.
Use Sonic Arrow to check a threatened approach or set up your team's next action. Save Storm Arrows for a target you can keep in view rather than spending them into protected space.
Dragonstrike can cut off a route or support a coordinated engagement. Pair its path with teammate pressure so enemies cannot avoid it at no cost.
illari: A survivor of the Inti Warriors who uses solar-powered support technology.
Place Healing Pylon behind cover where its healing can reach useful allies. Keep a backup position if enemies identify and destroy it.
Balance charged rifle pressure with your healing beam's resource. Outburst can create separation from a threat; do not spend it merely to move faster into danger.
Plan a Captive Sun engagement with teammate follow-up and an escape. Marking enemies is not enough if your team cannot safely apply the needed pressure.
junker-queen: The ruler of Junkertown, known for close-range combat and her axe.
Fight around corners where you can close distance without absorbing every ranged attack. Stay close enough for allies to help when you commit to a target.
Use Commanding Shout to support a meaningful engagement or retreat. Line up Carnage when enemies are actually within reach, rather than stepping into their whole team for one hit.
Rampage needs a route, a target group, and teammate follow-up. Track defensive answers to healing denial and avoid ending the charge beyond your team's support.
junkrat: A demolitionist whose explosives create pressure around obstacles.
Use bounced shots to pressure a route while keeping your body protected. A trap is most useful where an enemy has a reason to walk, not where it is easy to spot and shoot.
Reserve a Concussion Mine for movement if enemies can reach you. Avoid spending all your escape options to finish a target your team could safely pressure instead.
Start RIP-Tire from a position enemies cannot immediately reach. Choose a path that threatens a valuable group, and be ready to move your own body when the ultimate ends.
lifeweaver: The inventor of biolight, a technology that combines living forms with hard light.
Keep healing sightlines and use cover while charging Healing Blossom. A safe Petal Platform can give you or an ally a new angle without forcing a risky walk.
Life Grip changes another player's position. Watch the threat first and communicate a rescue plan, rather than interrupting a teammate's successful engagement.
Use Tree of Life to sustain a contested area your team can actually hold. Keep track of your allies' escape routes so your protection adds choices instead of replacing their judgment.
lucio: A musician and activist who supports his team through movement and music.
Move with allies who benefit from your current song. Wall Ride is a tool to keep useful angles and avoid pressure, not a reason to leave the team without support.
Choose healing or speed according to the team's immediate need. Amp It Up is stronger when it answers a committed move or a real recovery window.
Plan Sound Barrier around a dangerous enemy commitment and your allies' positions. Soundwave can separate an attacker from a vulnerable teammate without requiring a solo chase.
mauga: A Samoan fighter who uses heavy pressure and thrives in a direct confrontation.
Use cover while closing distance. Stay aware of support sightlines before Overrun carries you forward; reaching an enemy is not the same as being able to survive there.
Cardiac Overdrive rewards a fight your nearby allies can participate in. Use its window when targets are available and defensive resources have not already stopped your pressure.
Cage Fight can also trap you in a bad situation. Check who will be inside, who can support from outside, and whether your team is ready to commit.
mei: A climate scientist who uses ice technology to shape a fight.
Stay near cover and use your close pressure to protect an area your team can support. Long-range icicles let you contribute without walking into every enemy threat.
Use Ice Wall to isolate a reachable target or interrupt a threatening sightline. Avoid blocking an ally's escape or healing; be ready to remove an unhelpful wall.
Choose Blizzard when your team can pressure the area and follow up. Keep track of escape and defensive abilities, and use Cryo-Freeze from a position you can leave afterward.
moira: A genetic researcher whose methods are controversial and whose kit mixes healing and damage.
Maintain a position where your healing can reach multiple allies. Use damage safely to manage biotic resources; do not leave endangered teammates to pursue a distant target.
Choose the orb type for the current fight and consider how surfaces will affect its path. Keep Fade available when enemies have a realistic route to you.
Line up Coalescence to support allies and pressure enemies together. Track interruption threats and reposition through the beam's duration rather than standing in an exposed lane.
orisa: A robot built to protect Numbani and learning how to meet that responsibility.
Hold a corner and pressure a reachable target with the Fusion Driver. Let your weapon recover while cover protects you instead of staying exposed until every resource is gone.
Rotate Fortify and Javelin Spin according to the actual incoming threat. Use Energy Javelin to interrupt or displace a target your team can act on.
Terra Surge needs nearby targets and a safe commitment. Watch escape routes and teammate pressure; a long charge is not automatically better than an earlier release.
pharah: A soldier who uses flight equipment and explosive projectiles.
Use roofs and obstacles to limit how many enemies can see you. Manage your flight resources around a safe landing instead of staying in a predictable open position.
Pressure an angle where rockets force a useful movement. Keep Jet Dash or another movement option to answer a threatened sightline rather than using everything to approach.
Barrage leaves you committed to a position. Track interruption threats and use teammate pressure to create the opening; plan what happens immediately afterward.
ramattra: The leader of Null Sector who changes forms to control different engagement ranges.
Use Omnic pressure from a protected position and place the barrier to block a useful enemy line. Choose Nemesis when closing distance is realistic, not merely because it is available.
Use Ravenous Vortex on a route enemies need to cross. Plan where Nemesis pressure will finish so you can return to cover or support when the window ends.
Annihilation rewards staying in contact, but chasing beyond teammate sightlines can undo its value. Call the engagement and track enemy displacement or escape before committing.
reaper: A masked combatant whose identity and motives are shrouded in secrecy.
Use a route with cover to reach close range. Make sure Wraith Form can take you toward safety after the enemy notices you.
Shadow Step is a setup action, not a guarantee of surprise. Time your pressure with the front line so enemies must choose between more than one threat.
Death Blossom is vulnerable to defensive answers and interruption. Identify those resources before committing, and avoid giving up a safe close-range position for a low-value solo ultimate.
roadhog: A powerful enforcer who threatens nearby enemies with a hook and shotgun.
Play around cover with a hook angle your team can follow. The current Scrap Gun fires in two bursts, so maintain your aim through the attack instead of assuming the old firing pattern.
Trash Compactor answers projectile pressure, while Take a Breather supports recovery. Decide which threat you need to handle and do not spend both resources without an exit.
Whole Hog can displace enemies out of an area as well as deal damage. Consider where you are pushing the target and whether that direction helps your team's objective.
sigma: An astrophysicist whose gravity research left him with powers exploited by Talon.
Use Hyperspheres around cover at a range where their delayed explosion can matter. Move your barrier to address a useful sightline rather than leaving it in one place all fight.
Kinetic Grasp and the barrier answer different moments of pressure. Hold Accretion for an interrupt or target your teammates can punish, and avoid cycling every resource at once.
Gravitic Flux needs an engagement plan and awareness of interruption threats. Call the lifted targets and use safe positioning while your team prepares its follow-up.
sojourn: A former Overwatch leader determined to help its new generation avoid past mistakes.
Build pressure from an angle with a safe Power Slide route. Aim the stored-energy shot at a target you can reasonably hit rather than keeping energy while no useful target is in sight.
Use Disruptor Shot to contest a route or support your team's pressure. Save a movement choice if an enemy can reach your position while you are focusing on aim.
Overclock needs useful sightlines throughout its window. Change angles with your team and track defensive abilities that can deny a charged shot.
soldier-76: A wanted vigilante investigating the truth behind Overwatch's collapse.
Use Sprint to reach an angle with cover and a retreat path. Fire from a position that lets you keep a target in view without standing still in the open.
Place Biotic Field where it supports a real holding position. Use Helix Rockets when a target's movement or nearby surface makes the hit realistic.
Tactical Visor still requires enemies in view. Check barriers, cover, and defensive abilities before committing; moving to a better lane can matter more than activating immediately.
sombra: A hacker who uses information and, in the current Support kit, protective utility to influence a fight.
The current live role is Support. Keep Hotfix available for an ally under pressure, and use cover while applying short-range weapon pressure rather than following an old damage-only guide.
Cyberspace can help allies and weaken enemies in a contested area. Place its zone where both effects have a realistic use, and preserve Translocator for a safe reposition.
Coordinate EMP with teammate pressure. Watch which deployables you can disrupt and avoid making a deep ultimate engagement that leaves your team without support.
symmetra: A hard-light architect who uses constructs to shape movement and sightlines.
Use charged orbs when closing beam distance would expose you. Place turrets where they can reveal or pressure an approach without being immediately removed for free.
Tell teammates where a Teleporter goes before expecting them to use it. Protect its destination and keep an exit route when committing to close-range beam pressure.
Photon Barrier is strongest when it divides the enemy's useful sightlines while your allies can move and shoot around it. Think about the whole fight space, not just the target in front of you.
torbjorn: An engineer whose weapons and turret technology helped equip Overwatch.
Place the turret where it can cover a useful approach and survive ordinary sightline pressure. Use Rivet Gun yourself; repairing the turret is not always your best contribution.
Keep Overload for a threatening engagement or an opportunity you can safely use. Reposition the turret when the fight moves rather than defending an irrelevant old angle.
Spread Molten Core across paths enemies need to use. Avoid putting every pool in one spot that the whole team can simply walk around.
tracer: A former Overwatch pilot whose time-shifting equipment gives her unusual movement.
Take a covered approach and keep a Blink route away from danger. Pressure when teammates also demand attention, rather than entering alone before the fight begins.
Track where Recall will return you. Use short bursts of pressure to draw resources, and leave before a target's teammates can surround your current position.
Plan a Pulse Bomb approach around movement and defensive answers. Your goal is a reliable opportunity, not a deep commitment just because the ultimate is ready.
venture: An archaeologist and explorer who uses excavation equipment in combat.
Use cover to get within a useful range for the SMART Excavator. Start Burrow with an emergence route in mind instead of treating the underground state as a plan by itself.
Combine Drill Dash with a reachable target and a route back to support. Check where enemies will be when you emerge, and avoid spending every movement option to approach.
Tectonic Shock should threaten routes the enemy must hold or cross. Time it with teammate pressure so an opponent cannot simply back away from the whole engagement.
widowmaker: An assassin who uses patient long-range aim and strict control of sightlines.
Choose an angle where a missed shot does not leave you exposed to every opponent. Keep Grappling Hook for a needed reposition when the enemy discovers your location.
Use Venom Mine to watch an approach you cannot keep in your sights. Change firing angles after pressure or scouting reveals you instead of holding a predictable lane indefinitely.
Call information from Infra-Sight so your whole team can act on it. Track enemy movement abilities before committing to an exposed sniper angle.
wrecking-ball: A resourceful hamster engineer who turned a rolling mech into a fighting machine.
Learn a route into the fight and another route out. Use Grappling Claw to create an angle or displacement that your teammates can follow, not just to move quickly.
Use Piledriver when an enemy group is actually reachable and check interruption threats first. Adaptive Shield supports a commitment but does not replace an escape plan.
Minefield can control movement and objective access. Coordinate the space it denies with a teammate's pressure, and avoid leaving allies exposed while you chase a separate target.
zenyatta: An omnic monk who supports allies through spiritual orbs and precise projectile pressure.
Choose a covered position with a retreat corner and an ally who can help if you are approached. Keep Harmony on a teammate whose next action will expose them to pressure.
Call your Discord target so the team's pressure can align. Do not hold an open angle just to maintain an orb if enemy threats make that position unsafe.

Time Transcendence to answer a dangerous engagement that your allies can actually receive healing through. Track healing-denial effects and enemy displacement before relying on it as the whole defensive plan.
anran: A graduate of Wuxing University's Fire College who specializes in fire attacks.
Approach from cover with a route back to your team. Use your fire projectiles to establish pressure before committing movement toward an enemy.

Fan the Flames interacts with burning targets. Check that the target is affected before spending the follow-up, and use Dancing Blaze when nearby enemies make its defensive and healing effects useful.
Plan where Inferno Rush or Vermillion Ascent will leave you. If using Vermillion Revival, judge the surviving enemy pressure rather than assuming a return will make the original engagement safe.
domina: A Vishkar negotiator who uses hard-light barriers and controlled pressure.
Use the Barrier Array to divide useful enemy sightlines. Keep a covered position from which Photon Magnum can threaten a target without exposing your whole team.
Sonic Repulsors become more threatening around walls. Check the target's nearby geometry and line up an opportunity your allies can exploit instead of pushing a target out of their reach.
Plan a Crystal Charge detonation around enemy movement. Panopticon is a committed space-control tool; use it when teammate pressure can capitalize on the trapped area.
emre: A former Overwatch operative who returned after unexplained changes to his body and mind.
Use the Synthetic Burst Rifle from a protected angle. Aim and movement choices should keep a target available without making your own position predictable.
Cyber Frag has a bouncing trajectory. Choose a surface and follow-up target rather than throwing it into a route no enemy needs to use.
Override Protocol changes the commitment you can make. Review the form's current in-game mechanics before engaging and keep your team's sightlines in mind as you reposition.
freja: A former rescue operative who became a professional bounty hunter.
Use Take Aim from a position where slowing your movement is safe. Keep an escape or reposition option when enemies can see the angle you are using.
Quick Dash refreshes Take Aim in the official kit description. Plan the movement and follow-up shot together instead of dashing without a useful new angle.
Bola Shot can create a grouping opportunity. Use Updraft and your firing lane to time it with teammate pressure, while watching who can contest your airborne position.
hazard: An underworld disruptor who fights with spikes, movement, and a temporary wall.
Close distance using cover and short terrain access. Choose where Violent Leap will land before committing to close pressure.
Jagged Wall can alter a target's movement and sightlines. Place it to support your team's action rather than blocking allied healing or trapping yourself beyond cover.

Use Spike Guard against useful frontal pressure while tracking threats from other angles. Downpour creates an engagement opportunity that needs teammate follow-up, not a reason to leap alone into the whole enemy team.
jetpack-cat: A feline pilot using jet technology designed by Brigitte.
Use Biotic Pawjectiles from an angle that reaches allies while leaving an aerial escape. Keep terrain between you and enemy firing lanes rather than relying on flight alone.
Lifeline moves another player, so agree on a safe transport destination. Carrying an ally changes fuel recovery; budget Frenetic Flight around that commitment.
Use Purr where allies need its area healing and enemies can be displaced usefully. Catnapper changes an enemy's position; choose the landing and your own follow-up route before diving.
juno: A Martian-born support using space technology to protect her team and help her home.
Keep a line where Mediblaster can help allies and threaten enemies. Use hover and movement near cover rather than remaining in a steady open aerial position.
Pulsar Torpedoes need a useful lock-on opportunity. Place Hyper Ring on a route the team intends to use, and communicate that route instead of expecting a ring to create a plan on its own.
Orbital Ray moves through space. Start it along your team's intended engagement and keep Glide Boost for the repositioning that the moving fight requires.
mizuki: A fighter determined to escape a curse and control his own future.
Use Healing Kasa when its bounces can reach allies who need help. Keep a return position near cover before using Katashiro Return to advance.
Binding Chain can hinder an approaching threat. Coordinate the target with your team and avoid leaving your healing role just to pursue an isolated duel.
Place Kekkai Sanctuary where allies can use its healing and projectile protection. Consider incoming directions and escape routes; the sanctuary is not a guarantee against every attack type.
shion: An omnic who escaped Hashimoto captivity and became one of the clan's feared Elders.
Pressure from cover with Kira Pistols and preserve a route away from the target's teammates. Use movement to change the angle, not to stay indefinitely in close danger.
Execution's tighter spread requires a deliberate aiming window. Plan Joyride's dismount and launched-bike direction before committing to a contested route.
Satsuriku Spree commits a sequence of rushes. Track enemy control and escape options before starting, and think through where each rush leaves your own position.
sierra: A Helix Security teammate whose enhanced abilities support rifle pressure and movement.
Use sustained Helix Rifle fire from an angle with cover. The kit's accuracy behavior rewards keeping a realistic target in view, not standing exposed indefinitely.
Tracking Shot marks a target for rifle tracking. Choose a target your team can pressure and avoid tunneling on a mark that moved behind strong cover.
Place Anchor Drone to provide a useful grapple route before danger reaches you. Trailblazer's forward path should support an engagement or contested route your team can use.
vendetta: An Italian arena champion seeking control of her family's criminal legacy.
Approach through cover until the greatsword has a realistic target. Warding Stance addresses frontal pressure and consumes a resource, so do not rely on it to solve a surrounded position.
Plan Soaring Slice's destination and a safe follow-up. Whirlwind Dash creates a close commitment; check enemy movement and interruption threats before using both approach options.
Projected Edge spends defensive energy, so weigh its pressure against the protection you will need afterward. Coordinate Sundering Blade with teammates who can act on its frontal threat.
wuyang: A Water College support who uses healing technology and guided water attacks.
Keep Restorative Stream on an ally who needs sustained help. Aim water orbs from cover rather than letting guided aim distract you from approaching threats.
Manual healing consumes a resource. Balance it against the team's next emergency, and keep Rushing Torrent for a useful reposition when your angle becomes unsafe.
Use Guardian Wave to support an ally's engagement or displace an approaching threat. Tidal Blast protects a host and later detonates, so time the commitment with that delayed effect in mind.
dmon: The new leader of MEKA, a Korean mech team, who coordinates allies in close fighting.
Use Power Barrier to cover a useful approach while staying near hard cover. A frontal barrier does not protect every side of your mech.
Surging Strike requires the barrier stance. Plan that transition and use Propulsors with a landing route in mind, budgeting the fuel you will need to return to your team.

Limit Break creates a sweeping engagement opportunity that benefits from coordinated pressure. If the mech is lost, play the pilot's weapon and return-to-mech plan from safety rather than continuing the same frontline commitment.
doctrine: A cyberneticist who uses a drone fleet to control healing, pressure, and movement.
Use Eternal Scepter from a covered angle where you can help allies and pressure enemies. Watch the team's immediate support need before planning an offensive sequence.
Infuse changes the next ability. Choose that ability deliberately: an empowered attack, ally drones with self support, or a flight option can answer different threats.

Coordinate Deliverance with teammate pressure while monitoring who needs its protective overhealth. Shrouded Momentum can reposition you; keep a destination and an exit instead of using movement as a substitute for a safe plan.
